Rashi on Shabbat 115b:1:1.hebrew: אילימא ת"ק - כרב חסדא, ור' יוסי כרב הונא:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:1:1.english: If we say [it is] the first tanna - [he holds] like Rav Chisda, and Rabbi Yosei [holds] like Rav Huna.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:1:2.hebrew: דילמא - טעמא דת"ק משום דקסבר ניתנו לקרות בהן, ונהי דר' יוסי קאי כרב הונא, מיהו כרב חסדא לא קאי ולא חד, דהא רב חסדא אפי' למ"ד לא ניתנו קאמר מצילין:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:1:2.english: Perhaps - the reason of the first Tanna is that he holds they were permitted to be read; and although Rabbi Yosei accords with Rav Huna, nevertheless neither one accords with Rav Hisda, for Rav Hisda says [that] even according to the one who says they were not permitted [to be read], one rescues [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:1.hebrew: ומעניינות הרבה - מפרשיות שהיו כותבין בקמיעין פסוקים ללחש, כגון "כל המחלה" וכגון "לא תירא מפחד לילה":
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:1.english: And of many matters - [This refers to] passages from which they would write verses in amulets as an incantation, such as "All the diseases" and such as "You shall not fear the terror of night."

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:2.hebrew: הברכות - מטבע ברכות שטבעו חכמים, כגון י"ח ושאר ברכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:2.english: The blessings - The formula of blessings that the Sages instituted, such as the Eighteen [Benedictions] and other blessings.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:3.english: They burn in their place - If a fire breaks out on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:4.english: Like burners of Torah [scrolls] - For one may not rescue them on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:2:5.english: To examine him - [To see] whether the matter was true.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:1.english: [If] they were written - [This refers to] Torah, Prophets, and Writings.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:2.hebrew: תיבעי למ"ד - בנכתבים בכל לשון מצילין, תיבעי למ"ד אין מצילין:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:2.english: Let [the dilemma] be raised according to the one who says - [that] regarding [scrolls] written in any language, one rescues [them]; [and] let [the dilemma] be raised according to the one who says one does not rescue [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:3.english: That does not endure - [It] does not endure like ink.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:4.english: Didn't Rav Hamnuna teach - [that] one rescues [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:5.english: What was taught - Where was it taught?

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:6.hebrew: מדקאמר מגילה בדיו - וקתני דהוא מן הדברים שבין ספרים למגילה, ש"מ שאר ספרים נכתבים בסם ובסיקרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:3:6.english: Since it states [that] a Megillah [must be written] in ink - and it teaches that this is one of the matters [that distinguish] between [other] books and a Megillah, learn from this [that] other books may be written in arsenic or in red paint.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:2.hebrew: פ"ה אותיות - זהו שיעור לספר תורה שנמחק או בלה להיות עומד בקדושתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:2.english: Eighty-five letters - This is [the minimum] measure for a Torah scroll that was erased or worn out to remain in its sanctity.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:3.hebrew: כגון פרשת ויהי בנסוע הארון - שהוא ספר לעצמו כדלקמן, ויש בה פ"ה אותיות:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:3.english: As in the portion of “And when the Ark traveled” - For it is a book unto itself, as [stated] below, and there are eighty-five letters in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:4.english: To gather - That a word remains here and a word in another place.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:5.english: What is [the ruling] - [Whether] to rescue them.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:6.hebrew: ותיבעי לך פרשת ויהי בנסוע הארון גופה - שנכתבה לבדה וחסרה אות, מהו להצילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:6.english: And raise a dilemma [regarding] the portion of "And when the Ark traveled" itself - [Meaning, a scroll] that was written by itself and is missing a letter: what is [the law regarding] rescuing it?

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:4:7.english: In which there is not [enough] to compile - And in that compilation itself, there are no Divine Names.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:1.hebrew: תרגום שבתורה - יגר שהדותא, ושבנביאים כגון כדנא תימרון להום (ירמיהו י׳:י״א), שכתבו מקרא; [א"נ] התרגום שבעזרא כתבו מקרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:1.english: Aramaic translation in the Torah - [This refers to] "Yegar Sahaduta," and [that which is] in the Prophets — such as "Kidenah teimerun lehom" [Thus shall you say to them] (Jeremiah 10:11) — that one wrote in Hebrew [lit., Scripture]; [or alternatively,] the Aramaic [passage] that is in Ezra, one wrote it in Hebrew.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:2.hebrew: כתב עברית - אותיות גדולות הן, ואין דומות לכתב אשורית, אף ע"פ שכתובין בלשון הקדש, אלא שכתב האותיות משונות:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:2.english: Hebrew script - They are large letters and do not resemble Assyrian script, even though they are written in the Holy Tongue; rather, the script of the letters is different.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:3.english: And needless to say, the Aramaic [that is] in Ezra, in Daniel, and in the Torah - That one wrote it [in] Aramaic as is proper.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:4.hebrew: להשלים - אם היה בו כדי ללקט, ותרגום זו משלימו, מצטרף ומצילין בשבילו:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:5:4.english: To complete - If there was in it [enough] to gather, and this Aramaic translation completes it, it combines [with it] and one rescues [it] on its account.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:6:1.hebrew: תיובתא דרב הונא - דמדקתני ללקט, מכלל דמפוזרות נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:6:1.english: A conclusive refutation of Rav Huna - For since [the baraita] teaches "to gather," it follows that they are scattered.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:6:2.hebrew: בתיבות - הא דקתני ללקט, דמשמע מפוזרות, לא ללקט אות ואות לבד, אלא ללקט תיבה שלימה, תיבה כאן ותיבה כאן, עד פ"ה אותיות. וכי פלגינין — באותיות המפוזרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:6:2.english: In words - That which [the baraita] teaches, "to gather," which implies [that they are] scattered, [does] not [mean] to gather [one] letter and [another] letter alone, but rather to gather a complete word — a word here and a word there — up to eighty-five letters. And when we disagree, [it is] regarding scattered [individual] letters.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:7:1.hebrew: עשה לה סימניות מלמעלה ומלמטה - להבדיל' מן הסמוכות לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 115b:7:1.english: He made signs for it above and below - To separate it from the [portions] adjacent to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 115b:7:2.english: Above and below - At the beginning and at the end [of] “And when the Ark traveled.”

Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:1.hebrew: היו כתובים בסם ובסיקרא כו' - משמע דפשיטא ליה שאין קורין בהן, דאי קורין בהן — פשיטא דמצילין, כדאמר לעיל. וקשה לרשב"א: דבסמוך משמע דפשיטא ליה לריש גלותא גופיה דקורין בהן, דקאמר "והתניא מצילין", והיינו ההוא ברייתא דמייתי: "שהספרים נכתבים בכל לשון, ומגילה עד שתהא כתובה אשורית על הספר ובדיו", אבל שאר ספרים נכתבין שלא בדיו. ולפי מה שאפרש בסמוך, דהך ברייתא איירי לענין הצלה, אתי שפיר, ולעולם אין קורין בהן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:1.english: [If] they were written in arsenic or red paint, etc. - This implies that it is obvious to him that one does not read from them, for if one reads from them — it is obvious that one rescues [them], as stated above. And Rashba finds [this] difficult: for immediately below it is implied that it is obvious to the Exilarch himself that one does read from them, as he says, "And was it not taught in a baraita that one rescues [them]?" And this refers to that baraita that [the Gemara] cites: "that the books [of Scripture] are written in any language, and a Megillah [is not valid] unless it is written in Assyrian [script], on a scroll, and in ink" — [implying that] other books, however, may be written without ink. And according to what I will explain immediately below, that this baraita is speaking about the matter of rescuing [from a fire], it works out well, and in fact one does not read from them.

Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:2.hebrew: אבל הכא כיון דלא מקיים לא - אע"ג דבפ"ב דגיטין (דף יט.) קרי להו דבר שמתקיים, דתנן: "בכל כותבין, בסם ובדיו ובסקרא ובקומוס ובקנקנתום ובכל דבר שמתקיים", אומר ר"י דהתם קרי ליה מתקיים טפי ממשקין ומי פירות דקתני התם בסיפא דאין כותבין בהן, אבל אין מתקיימין כמו דיו. אבל קשה לר"י, דתנן בפ"ב דסוטה (דף יז:) גבי מגילת סוטה: "אין כותבין לא בקומוס ולא בקנקנתום, שנאמר ומחה — כתב שיכול למחוק", אלמא קומוס וקנקנתום מתקיימין יותר מדיו! ואומר ר"י דלעולם אין מתקיימין כמו דיו, ואין יכול למחות כמו דיו לפי שנבלעין בקלף:
Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:2.english: "However, here, since [the script] does not endure, [they are] not [rescued]" - Although in the second chapter of Gittin (19a) it calls them something that endures — as we learned in a Mishnah: "With anything one may write [a bill of divorce]: with arsenic, with ink, with red paint, with gum, with iron sulfate, or with anything that endures" — Rabbi Yitzchak says that there it calls it enduring relative to liquids and fruit juices, which it teaches there in the latter clause that one may not write with them, but they do not endure like ink. However, Rabbi Yitzchak has a difficulty, for we learned in a Mishnah in the second chapter of Sotah (17b) regarding the sotah scroll: "One may not write [it] neither with gum nor with iron sulfate, as it is stated: 'and he shall erase' — [requiring] writing that can be erased," which proves that gum and iron sulfate endure more than ink! And Rabbi Yitzchak says that in truth they do not endure like ink, yet one cannot erase [them] like ink because they are absorbed into the parchment.

Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:3.hebrew: מגילה עד שתהא כתובה אשורית על הספר ובדיו - משמע דשאר ספרים לא בעי ספר ודיו. וקשה, דבפ' המוציא יין (לעיל שבת דף עט:) משמע דספר תורה בעי ספר, דתני': "על הנייר ועל המטלית — פסולה", ומוקי לה בס"ת. וה"ה על הדיפתרא: אע"ג דלא חשיב ליה לענין פסול, ה"נ לא חשיב ליה לענין כשרות, דקתני: "על הקלף ועל הדוכסוסטוס — כשירה", ולא קתני דיפתרא. ועוד, תנן במסכת סופרים (פ"א): "אין כותבין לא ע"ג דיפתרא ולא ע"ג נייר מחוק". ועוד, דמגילה פסולה אדיפתרא כדתנן פ"ב דמגילה (דף יז.), וכן מגילת סוטה פסולה אדיפתרא כדאמר בפ"ב דסוטה (דף יז:), משום דבעיא ספר; וכ"ש ס"ת, דנקראת כמה פעמים "ספר". ודיו נמי צריך, כדאמר בפרק הבונה (לעיל שבת קג:): "כתבה שלא בדיו, או שכתב האזכרות בזהב — הרי אלו יגנזו". ותירץ הרב יוסף, דס"ת ודאי בעי ספר ודיו, והכא איירי דווקא בשאר ספרים; והא דלא קתני "אין בין ספרים לס"ת ומגילה" — משום דס"ת נכתבים בכל לשון, להכי לא עריב לה. ואכתי קשה לר"י: דתנן בפ"ק דמגילה (דף ח:): "אין בין ספרים לתפילין ומזוזות אלא שהספרים נכתבין בכל לשון כו'"; ופריך בגמרא: "וספרים נכתבין בכל לשון? ורמינהו: מקרא שכתבו תרגום, ותרגום שכתבו מקרא, וכתב עברי — אינו מטמא את הידים עד שיכתבנו בכתב אשורית, על הספר ובדיו". ומשני: "כאן בספרים, כאן במגילה". ורב אשי משני: "כי תניא ההיא בשאר ספרים, ורבי יהודה היא". אלמא בשאר ספרים נמי בעי רבי יהודה ספר ודיו, והוא הדין לרבנן, דלא אשכחן דפליגי רבנן עליה אלא בכתב אשורית, אבל בספר ודיו לא אשכחן דפליגי. ועוד קשה, דשביק רב אשי התם שינויא קמא דמוקי לה במגילה, ומסייע ליה ברייתא דהכא דקתני בהדיא דמגילה בעי שתהא כתובה אשורית וספר ודיו, ורב אשי גופיה מייתי לה הכא. ונראה לר"י, דדוקא לענין הצלה מיתניא הך ברייתא ד"אין בין ספרים למגילה אלא שהספרים נכתבין בכל לשון", ואפי' בלא ספר ודיו חשיבו לענין דמצילין אותו מפני הדליקה אע"ג דלא חזו לקריאה, משום דיש בהו אזכרות; אבל במגילה — אין מצילין אלא א"כ ראויה לקריאה, שתהא כתובה אשורית על הספר ובדיו, לפי שאין בה הזכרה. וא"ת: א"כ, תקשה מברייתא דהכא דאמר לעיל "כל היכא דלא ניתנו לקרות בהן אין מצילין"? וי"ל: דהא מסיק לעיל "תנאי היא":
Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:3:3.english: "The Megillah [is not valid] until it is written in Assyrian [script], on a scroll, and in ink" - This implies that other books [of Scripture] do not require a [parchment] scroll and ink. Yet this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] Hamotzi Yayin (earlier, Shabbat 79b), it is implied that a Torah scroll requires a [parchment] scroll, as it was taught [in a baraita]: "On papyrus or on a rag — it is invalid," and [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring] to a Torah scroll. And the same applies [to writing] on diftara [partially processed hide]: even though [the baraita] does not list it with respect to invalidity, so too it does not list it with respect to validity, as it teaches: "On klaf or on duchsustos — it is valid," and it does not teach diftara. Furthermore, we learned in Tractate Soferim (ch. 1): "One may not write either on diftara or on erased papyrus." Furthermore, a Megillah [written] on diftara is invalid, as we learned in the second chapter of Megillah (17a), and likewise a Sotah scroll is invalid [if written] on diftara, as it says in the second chapter of Sotah (17b), because it requires a "sefer" [scroll]; and all the more so a Torah scroll, which is called a "sefer" several times! And ink is also required, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Haboneh (earlier, Shabbat 103b): "If one wrote it without ink, or wrote the Divine Names in gold — these must be stored away." And Rav Yosef resolved [this]: A Torah scroll certainly requires a [parchment] scroll and ink, and here [the baraita] is speaking specifically of other books [of Scripture]. And the reason it does not teach "There is no difference between books [of Scripture] and a Torah scroll and a Megillah" is because Torah scrolls [too, according to the Tanna of that baraita,] are written in any language; therefore it did not group it [with the Megillah]. Yet it is still difficult to R"i: for we learned in the first chapter of Megillah (8b): "The only difference between books [of Scripture] and tefillin and mezuzot is that books are written in any language, etc." And the Gemara asks: "Are books [of Scripture] written in any language? Contrast this [with a baraita]: [A verse of] Scripture that one wrote in Aramaic translation, or an Aramaic translation that one wrote in Hebrew, or [in] Paleo-Hebrew script — it does not render the hands impure unless one writes it in Assyrian script, on a scroll, and in ink." And [the Gemara] answers: "Here [it refers] to books [of Scripture], [and] here [it refers] to the Megillah." And Rav Ashi answers: "When that [baraita] was taught, it was regarding other books [of Scripture], and it is [the view of] Rabbi Yehudah." Thus, even for other books [of Scripture], Rabbi Yehudah requires a [parchment] scroll and ink, and the same applies to the Rabbis — for we do not find that the Rabbis disagree with him except regarding Assyrian script, whereas regarding a [parchment] scroll and ink we do not find that they disagree. Furthermore, it is difficult why Rav Ashi there abandons the first answer that establishes it [as referring] to the Megillah, when the baraita here supports him, as it explicitly teaches that a Megillah requires that it be written in Assyrian [script], on a scroll, and in ink — and Rav Ashi himself cites it here! Therefore, it appears to R"i that this baraita — "The only difference between books [of Scripture] and a Megillah is that books are written in any language" — was taught specifically with regard to saving [from a fire on Shabbat]: even without a [parchment] scroll and ink, they are significant enough that we save them from a fire, even though they are not fit for [ritual] reading, because they contain Divine Names. However, in the case of a Megillah, we do not save [it] unless it is fit for [ritual] reading — that it be written in Assyrian [script], on a scroll, and in ink — because there is no mention of the Divine Name in it. And if you ask: If so, let there be a difficulty from the baraita here, as [the Gemara] said earlier: "Wherever they were not given to be read from, we do not save [them]"? One can answer: Earlier [the Gemara] concluded, "It is a dispute among Tannaim."

Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:6:1.hebrew: מיתיבי ס"ת שבלה אם יש בה כדי ללקט כו' - השתא משמע דמלשון "ללקט" קא פריך, דמשמע אפי' מפוזרות. ותימה: א"כ, אמאי קא בעי מעיקרא "מכונסות או אפ' מפוזרות"? פשיטא דאפי' מפוזרות! מדבעא רב הונא "ס"ת שאין בו ללקט", משמע: הא יש בו ללקט — מצילין, אע"פ שהן מפוזרות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 115b:6:1.english: [The Gemara] raises an objection: A Torah scroll that is worn, if there is enough in it to compile, etc. - At this point, it is implied that [the Gemara] is raising its objection from the term "to compile," which implies even [when the letters are] scattered. And this is astonishing: if so, why did [the Gemara] ask initially [whether they must be] juxtaposed or [may be] even scattered? It is obvious that [they may be] even scattered! Since Rav Huna asked [earlier regarding] "a Torah scroll in which there is not [enough] to compile," this implies: if there is [enough] in it to compile — one rescues [it], even though they are scattered.
